'''''Doronicum plantagineum''''', the '''plantain-leaved leopard's-bane'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=17 October 2014 }}</ref> or '''plantain false leopardbane''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=DOPL|taxon=Doronicum plantagineum|accessdate=18 January 2016}}</ref> is a European plant species in the [[Asteraceae|sunflower family]]. It is native to southeastern Europe from Greece and Italy to Ukraine and the Czech Republic.<ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=doronicum+plantagineum Altervista Flora Italiana, Doronico piantagineo, Wegerich-Gämswurz, stor gemsrot, ''Doronicum plantagineum'' L.]</ref> There are reports of the species being naturalized in the State of [[Oregon]] in the northwestern United States.<ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Doronicum%20plantagineum.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref>

''Doronicum plantagineum'' is a perennial herb up to 80 cm (2 feet) tall. Leaves are roundish, up to 11 cm (4.4 inches) long. The plant creates yellow flower heads one at a time, each up to 5 cm (2 inches) in diameter and containing both fay florets and disc florets.<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=110834 Flora of North America, Plantain-leaved leopard’s-bane, ''Doronicum plantagineum'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 885. 1753. ]</ref>

;Subspecies<ref name=l/>

*''Doronicum plantagineum'' subsp. ''emarginatum'' <small>(H.J.Coste) P.Fourn.</small>
*''Doronicum plantagineum'' subsp. ''plantagineum''
*''Doronicum plantagineum'' subsp. ''tournefortii'' <small>(Rouy) Cout.</small>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''plantagineum'' refers to the leaves of the plant which are similar to those of a [[plantago|plantain]].<ref>W. T. Parsons, William Thomas Parsons and E. G. Cuthbertson {{Google books|sRCrNAQQrpwC|Noxious Weeds of Australia|page=325}}</ref>
